title: Episode 76 — The Red Zone with Steve Lee
summary: Episode 76 is both Steve Lee's early public creative record and a case study in consent that occurs too late. He performs his developing cowboy-rap routine, discusses three months of open mics, five years of recovery, wrestling, family caregiving and the support/dependence loop with his brother Bobby. But after the room has already elicited drugs, knife threats, job loss and sexual history, Steve says he expected only to meet the group, did not know he would be on the podcast, and did not expect to bare his soul. The host answers that entering the garage made recording inevitable and that it is too late. The archive rejects that premise and gives Steve's stop/hesitation statements editorial force. Childhood-abuse details, an alleged disabled perpetrator, private relatives, recovery specifics and medical history are minimized beyond the creator chronology Steve chooses to make public. The title's red zone connects competitive gaming rage, sibling knife display, a theater confrontation, wrestling-performance fear and Critter's reported fight history; emotional flooding may explain conduct but never excuses threats or assault. The final major sequence turns an unhoused woman's blanket barrier into a proposed sex-for-shelter ultimatum, physical removal lesson, hair-dragging instruction, arson joke and deception plan. Every branch is rejected: hospitality creates no sexual entitlement; housing need makes consent more constrained, not less; a refusal ends sexual contact; and safe removal must not become retaliation or violence. The episode also resolves Justin Chan's 2013 PolicyMic article, identifies Choi Min-sik and key songs, corrects cataract surgery, safer sex-toy use, suicide statistics and masturbation myths, and documents Kalilah's episode-era naming plus the 500-copy Into the Limelight vinyl promotion. Named dialogue remains withheld.
sensitivity: Surprise recording and publication consent; childhood sexual abuse and alleged grooming; disability slurs and guessed diagnosis; sibling violence, knives and assault; threats toward children and fans; recovery and substance use; suicide statements and statistics; unhoused-person sexual coercion, expulsion, assault and arson; private partners and family medical history; explicit sexual content; minors' sexual history; racial and orientation slurs; informal family labor and financial dependence.
speaker_policy: Named dialogue remains withheld. Episode 76 has zero diarized turns and five coarse window embeddings for a changing ensemble. Public participants are contextually known, but no independently held-out multispeaker validation has passed.
